wholeProduct.summary: Extend the existing TradeScout business directory with a source-backed stone-industry corridor from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, through Panama City, Florida, while preserving profile ownership, public-contact boundaries, and the existing JW Stone anchor.

deliverables.outcome: Prepare 51 official-source business-location profiles covering stone fabricators, suppliers, and installers across the Baton Rouge-to-Panama City corridor, with county routing and internal JW Stone/BidRock targeting metadata.
deliverables.entry: Use official business websites to identify a real corridor location and its public business facts.
deliverables.ending: A validated CSV row can enter the canonical staging pipeline as an unclaimed, draft business profile without inventing trust claims or overwriting a claimed profile.
constraints: Interpret Panama as Panama City, Florida.
Treat JW Stone as the existing corridor anchor and do not create a duplicate JW Stone row.
Use only public business facts from an official business website for the source-backed roster.
Do not assert a TradeScout partnership, verification, license status, review count, or rating.
Reuse the canonical stage-business-csv and merge-staged-businesses pipeline, business records, county mappings, public profile routes, Businesses workspace, and claim flow.
Never overwrite owner-authored fields on a claimed profile; on an existing unclaimed profile, fill only missing public fields.
Keep researched acquisition and JW Stone/BidRock fit metadata internal to importExtras.
Keep imported records in draft status until a separate public-activation approval.
Do not expose direct contact information or bypass Intent to Decision Card to Contact gating.
Do not create fake CRM contacts or named decision-makers from generic public business data.
excludedFromActive: Claiming profiles on behalf of businesses.
Changing public profile, search, contact, trust, ranking, or claim UX.
Publishing, deploying, importing into a remote database, or activating draft records before explicit approval.
proofRequired: Dataset contract proves 51 unique locations, official-source domain alignment, complete county routing, role and market coverage, and no invented trust claims.
Importer contract proves public field mapping, internal targeting metadata, fill-only-missing behavior, and claimed-profile preservation.
Adjacent claim-import and public-profile contract suites pass.
Typecheck, minimum-release gate, production build, and git diff checks pass at the implementation state.
A production import must run preflight and dry-run before any draft merge; activation remains a distinct approved action.

executionTarget.rationale: TradeScout already owns the business directory, profile claim model, public routes, county scope, import pipeline, search workspace, and gated contact flow.

baseline.productionObservation: No remote database mutation, public activation, outreach, push, merge, or deployment was performed during local preparation.
